verses.1: The words that came from Jehovah to Jeremiah: “Babylon’s king Nebuchadnezzar, and all his army, and all the kings of the land under his rule, are fighting against Jerusalem and all its cities.”
verses.2: As the LORD, the God of Israel, said: “I will give this city into the hands of King Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.”
verses.3: And you shall not be taken away by force. You will be released, and in his hands you will be given over to him. Your eyes will see the eyes of Babylon’s king. He will speak through your mouth, and Babylon will come upon you.
verses.4: But listen to the words of Jehovah, the righteous king of Judah! As Jehovah said, “Do not die in that place.”
verses.5: In peace shall you rest, just as your ancestors, the kings who came before you, rested. So also shall you rest. May God bless you, for I have spoken these words. Amen.
verses.6: And the prophet Jeremiah spoke to Zedekiah, king of Judah, about all these things in Jerusalem.
verses.7: And the army of Babylon fought against Jerusalem and all the cities of Judah that were still under their control. They went to Lachish and Azekah, because those cities remained under Jewish control.
verses.8: The message that came to Jeremiah from Jehovah, after the king Zedekiah’s death, was a covenant with all the people living in Jerusalem. It was a command to them to obey God’s laws.
verses.9: To send a man his servant and his Hebrew wife. The Hebrew woman is a person who seeks no other husband than the Jewish man with whom she can live.
verses.10: And all the messengers and all the people who came to make a covenant with God, and who wanted to send someone as their servant or someone from their family, were willing to serve them no longer. And they listened, and sent them away.
verses.11: And after that, they returned. They made those servants and maids who had been sent away as vagrants become their own servants and maids.
verses.12: And the word of Jehovah was spoken to Jeremias from Jehovah himself:
verses.13: As Jehovah, the God of Israel, says: “I have made a covenant with your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.”
verses.14: After seventy years, you shall send one of your Hebrew brothers to be sold to you as a slave. He shall serve you for six years. Then you shall release him from your service. But your ancestors did not listen to me, and they did not open their ears to me.
verses.15: And today, you shall do what is right in my eyes. You shall read the laws and regulations for each other. And you shall make a covenant before me in the house where my name is mentioned.
verses.16: And they returned, and they polluted my name. Each man took back his servant and his wife, whom you sent out as free people for their own souls. They made them your servants and wives.
verses.17: Therefore, thus says the LORD: You have not listened to me when I called for help from one person to another. I call upon you now, in the name of the LORD, against famine, against starvation. I will give you over to all the kings of the earth.
verses.18: And I gave them the people who carried the covenant stones. They did not make the words of the covenant themselves. They were given those words by God before the calf was sacrificed. Those words were given to them so that they could carry them among their people.
verses.19: The priests of Judah and Jerusalem, the scribes and priests, and all the people of the land who traveled between the gates of the city.
verses.20: And I will hand them over to their enemies, and to those who seek to destroy them. They will become food for the birds in the sky, and for the animals on the earth.
verses.21: And Ether of Judah, and his servants, they shall be given over to their enemies, to those who seek to harm them. They shall also be given over to the army of king Babylon, who will take them away from you.
verses.22: I command you, O LORD! Return to this city, and fight against it. Burn it down with fire. And make all the cities of Judah completely uninhabitable.
